# Squidbrake

> Squidbrake is change control for AI agents: agents propose, people approve. It checks every tool call an AI agent makes against your rules and what the agent already did, and allows it, holds it for a second person (with what it will change shown first, such as rows deleted or resources destroyed), or blocks it, before the call runs. Approved deletes can be undone, and decisions land in a tamper-evident log with a one-page evidence pack for auditors. Decisions come from rules, not an LLM.

Squidbrake runs where you run it: a laptop, Docker, or your own cloud. It is backed by Entrepreneurs First.

## Start here

- [This site as markdown](https://squidbrake.com/index.md): what Squidbrake does, the incidents it was tested on, how policy works, measured latency, FAQ
- [Quickstart](https://squidbrake.com/docs): install, connect agents, write a policy, block a call
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/squidbrake/): `pipx install squidbrake`
- [Pricing](https://squidbrake.com/pricing): open source free to self-host; hosted Free (watch only, 2,000 actions/month), Starter $9/month, Pro $19/month, Team $299/month (up to 10 people, 14-day trial), Scale $499/month (up to 50 people), Enterprise priced with you; what is not built yet
- [Security](https://squidbrake.com/security): where it runs, what it stores, how secrets and keys are kept, what it can't stop, compliance mapping (SOC 2 CC8.1, ISO 27001 A.8.32 and A.8.15, EU AI Act Art. 12 and 14), reporting a vulnerability
- [Changelog](https://squidbrake.com/changelog): every release, newest first

## What it connects to

Coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code Copilot, Antigravity), agents that connect to MCP by URL (ChatGPT and claude.ai connectors, Devin, n8n), agent frameworks (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, PydanticAI, smolagents, Google ADK), and any MCP server. Support, finance and ops agents go through the same rules as coding agents.

## Evidence

- [Benchmark write-up](https://squidbrake.com/benchmark): 16 public AI-agent incidents replayed against the shipped rules (last run 14 Nov 2026, v0.14.23). 17 of 20 harmful actions stopped, the three misses documented. Code: [incidents](https://github.com/batrapulkit/squidbrake/tree/main/incidents), `python incidents/replay.py`.
- [Session benchmark](https://github.com/batrapulkit/squidbrake/tree/main/bench/chains): 66 agent sessions, 118 steps. Squidbrake on whole sessions stopped 68 of 71 harmful steps and held 3 of 41 routine ones; an allowlist stopped 55 and held 10; asking for everything held 40.
- [Default policy](https://github.com/batrapulkit/squidbrake/blob/main/rules.yaml): the rules Squidbrake ships with

## Guides

- [AI agent governance: a practical framework for teams putting agents in production](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-governance-framework): A practical AI agent governance framework: inventory, identity, least privilege, approvals, a kill switch, an audit trail and a weekly review.
- [Audit trails for AI agents: what to log, and how to make the record tamper-evident](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-audit-trail): What an AI agent audit trail should record (who asked, what ran, who approved), why traces aren't enough, and how to make the log tamper-evident.
- [Securing Claude Code for your team: managed settings, permissions, hooks and approvals](https://squidbrake.com/blog/claude-code-enterprise-security): Rolling Claude Code out to a team? Managed settings, allow, ask and deny rules, turning off bypass mode, hooks, sandboxing, MCP allowlists and an audit trail.
- [Least privilege for AI agents: credentials, tools and what an agent should never hold](https://squidbrake.com/blog/least-privilege-ai-agents): AI agents inherit whatever credentials sit on the machine. How to apply least privilege: per-agent identities, scoped tokens, secrets out of reach and fewer tools.
- [AI agent kill switch: how to stop a runaway agent, and what to set up before you need one](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-kill-switch): When an AI agent loops, burns budget or starts deleting things, how do you stop it fast? Kill switches, spend limits, circuit breakers and what to check after.
- [AI coding agent policy: a template for engineering teams (2026)](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-coding-agent-policy-template): A copy-ready AI coding agent policy for engineering teams: approved tools, data rules, what agents may do alone, what needs a person, and how to enforce it.
- [Claude Code deleted my files: how to get them back, and stop it next time](https://squidbrake.com/blog/claude-code-deleted-my-files)
- [YOLO mode in Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, compared (2026)](https://squidbrake.com/blog/yolo-mode-claude-code-cursor-codex)
- [9 seconds: how a token an AI agent found deleted a production database and its backups](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-found-a-token-pocketos)
- [Vibe coding security: 10 checks before you ship (2026)](https://squidbrake.com/blog/vibe-coding-security-checklist)
- [Stop AI agents force-pushing to main: branch protection, hooks and approvals](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-git-force-push)
- [Approval fatigue: why asking about every agent action makes you less safe](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-approval-fatigue)
- [How an AI agent deleted a production database, and how to stop it](https://squidbrake.com/blog/ai-agent-deleted-production-database)
- [Human-in-the-loop approval for AI agents](https://squidbrake.com/blog/human-in-the-loop-approval-for-ai-agents)
- [MCP security checklist](https://squidbrake.com/blog/mcp-security-checklist)
